newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel falls to an 18-month low.
newsitem.headline: SingTel falls to an 18-month low.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) shares slid to an 18-month low of Singapore S$2.76 on Thursday.
The last time SingTel shares was at S$2.76 was on September 27, 1995.
At 0735 GMT, the shares were trading around S$2.80, down S$0.18 on a healthy turnover of over 2.8 million shares.
Analysts told Reuters SingTel stock came under pressure because it lost the monopoly in Singapore's mobile phone and pager markets on April 1.

"Basically, they have to compete to maintain their market share. Operating costs are going to increase as more has to be spent on advertisements and attractive offers. This is going to eat into margins," said an analyst with a local brokerage.
On Wednesday, SingTel launched cheaper cellular phone services and packages to match rivals' packages.
Analysts said they did not expect SingTel shares to slide below S$2.50.

"The support will be at S$2.50. That's the maximum it will go because Singaporeans were offered some shares at that level. It will be too much for the government's pride if the share price went below this," said another analyst.
Last year, Singapore government investment arm Temasek Holdings issued 804 million shares at S$2.50 each to 1.53 million Singaporeans in the second tranche offered.
Another five million shares were issued to self-help groups. -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703083)
